sections.overview: The Rannoch Looper is a geometrid moth recorded here under the catalogue name Macaria brunneata; a 2024 molecular revision transferred it to Speranza.
sections.identification: In Britain, adults are day-flying and often rest with their wings held closed like a butterfly.
sections.habitat: In Britain it is associated with mature woodland in central Scotland, although occasional migrants are recorded farther south.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on bilberry, Vaccinium myrtillus.
sections.behavior: Adults appear in June and July in Britain and fly by day.
sections.reproduction: The available accounts identify bilberry as the larval food plant but do not establish clutch size or brood number.
sections.ecology: Older checklists grouped it with Epelis carbonaria under Macaria, but recent molecular taxonomy places them in separate genera.
sections.conservation: Butterfly Conservation assigns the Rannoch Looper medium threat priority in its Scotland strategy; this is a regional planning priority, not a global Red List category.
